root_idea.summary: The root has two principal orientations: thinness or delicacy, opposed to coarseness and hardness, and the movement or shimmering of a fluid.
root_idea.development: From thinness come meanings such as shallow, attenuated, weak, scant, delicate, and parchment or thin bread; from fluid movement come flowing, undulating, glittering, and tears moving at the eyelid.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic noun has an independently attested parchment or writing-material sense.

senses.definition: Parchment, vellum, or another writing sheet; by extension, an inscribed record or book. In the Quranic expression, it is understood as the written or revealed record spread open.
senses.usage_conditions: Occurs in فِي رَقٍّ مَنْشُورٍ, describing writing material or the written/revealed record laid open. Interpretations identifying the object with a revealed Book or record remain within this writing-material sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become thin, fine, delicate, flimsy, shallow, or attenuated; رَقِيقٌ denotes something having little thickness or depth and, of bread, something thin and spread out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to material substances, water, sand, mud, garments, bread, and similar things. This is the physical thinness branch, distinct from later figurative applications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weakness or abjectness resulting from attenuation, especially weakness of bones or bodily structure; also weak, mean, paltry, or contemptible.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes weakened bones and bodily structure and the figurative description of a person or possession as weak or lowly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Paucity, scantness, or a small remaining amount, including scant property, food, sustenance, or years.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of diminution; the evidence applies it to property, food, living, and the remainder of one's years.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weak-heartedness, fearfulness, bashfulness, or a disposition lacking firmness or resistance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the soul, heart, or a person's disposition; it can also describe weakness in religion or resolve.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feel compassion, mercy, or pity for someone; tender-hearted or receptive to admonition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction رَقَّ لَهُ takes the person toward whom compassion is felt; tender-heartedness is opposed to hardness or cruelty of heart.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Soft, graceful, elegant, easy, sweet, or ornate speech and expression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to the quality of words, language, or expression rather than to the physical thinness of an object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have or make a slender, soft, or gentle voice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional application to the sound or quality of the voice.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A narrow, bad, or difficult state of affairs; scant or straitened living.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person's circumstances, condition, livelihood, or sustenance, not merely of physical thinness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Slavery, servitude, or the condition of being a slave.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct nominal branch from the parchment sense of رَقٌّ; it denotes the legal or social condition rather than a physical quality.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make, take, keep, or possess someone as a slave; made or kept as a slave.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transitive verb denotes bringing someone into slavery, while the passive-derived adjective describes the resulting status.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tortoise or other specified aquatic reptile, including a crocodile in some descriptions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A zoological homonym; descriptions and classification vary among authorities, and the plural is رُقُوقٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Shallow or non-abundant water; water that has become shallow and has mostly sunk into the earth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to water in a sea, great river, valley, or similar place; related descriptions may refer to water receding or disappearing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Leaves or easily eaten branches of trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plant-related use describing foliage suitable for cattle to eat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain thorny plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical use reported independently from the meaning ‘thin thing’ or ‘leaves’.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land beside a valley over which water spreads and into which it later sinks, producing good herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographical term for a water-affected strip or tract beside a valley.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a white grape, to become thin-skinned and rich in juice, or to become fully ripe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form IV use applied to the white grape.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For dispositions to become niggardly, tenacious, or avaricious.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use describing a change in people's natural dispositions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To captivate someone so that his patience or endurance becomes weak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction describes an influence that weakens a person's endurance; the source's illustrative subject does not impose a gender restriction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a traditional idiom, to come to or choose some eventual state or course of mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The idiom's derivation is explicitly uncertain; this meaning is retained as a reported lexical use rather than treated as a regular productive sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the night, to pass for the most part.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form X use describing the diminution or passing away of a period of time.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour or let a liquid flow in small quantity, to spread it over something, or for a liquid to run easily.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to water and other liquids, including pouring fat or perfume over food or cloth; the intransitive form describes liquid or something similar flowing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mix or dilute wine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized transitive use applied to wine or a similar liquid.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make the eye shed tears, or for tears to gather and move at the inner edge of the eyelid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transitive and intransitive usages describe causing tears and the movement of tears respectively.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To embellish, invest with charm, or make one thing lead attractively to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used figuratively of speech, allurement, or successive acts of sedition that make one another desirable.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To move to and fro, undulate, flicker, or come and go; recurrent or apparent motion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to water, mirage, clouds, tears, the sun near the horizon, and other things whose motion appears recurrent or wavering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To shine, glisten, or appear to shimmer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to mirage, sunlight, and other shining things; apparent motion and shining may overlap in descriptions of mirage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A graceful or indirect allusion, including using a mild expression such as ‘kissing’ as a euphemism for sexual intercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional rhetorical use: the wording is softened or made courteous while referring indirectly to another act.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The pronunciation of a sound with a slender quality, opposed to emphatic pronunciation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical recitation term, especially concerning the slender pronunciation of the long fatḥa and of lām, opposed to تَفْخِيمٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a gait easy, or to go at an easy pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited usage is especially applied to the movement of a camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To create or excite disorder, disagreement, dissension, or mischief among people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative social use with بَيْنَ describing disruption between or among a group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thin, flat, expanded bread; a single thin round cake.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: رُقَاقٌ may function substantivally, while مُرَقَّقٌ describes bread made thin and broad.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A level, broad tract of soft land, often with harder ground beneath it, including a desert tract from which water has sunk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographical term for expanded soft terrain; variants and closely related forms are reported in the same lexical family.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hot day.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional descriptive use, apparently associated with the day's bright or intense sunlight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman or girl whose complexion shines or glistens, as though water were running over her face.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive epithet for a lustrous complexion; the source's gender is intrinsic to this lexical noun, not a restriction on the wider root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sword with abundant lustre or wavy markings, or one that shines greatly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive use for a sword's surface or brilliance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mirage or beverage described as shallow or thin, according to variant readings and interpretations.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence reports a textual and lexical uncertainty between a mirage-related reading and a beverage-related reading; neither is treated as a Quranic use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The finest or most delicate piece of fat; by extension, something easily approached or taken advantage of.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: رُقَّى is the feminine form in the cited expression and occurs in a proverb about a person regarded as weak or readily exploitable.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thin or soft anatomical part, including the regions between the flank and groin, the lower belly, the sides of the nose, or comparable delicate folds and surfaces.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical use; the exact body region varies by construction and is not reduced to a single modern anatomical term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thinness or lightness in a horse's hoof.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized zoological description of the hoof rather than a general statement about the animal's condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Looseness of the bowels or diarrhea.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized bodily use of رِقَّةٌ in the expression رِقَّةُ بَطْنٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cattle disposed or appearing to be near fatness, leanness, or perishing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a herd's visibly changing or precarious condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A baker's rolling pin or other implement used to make bread thin and flat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete tool noun derived from the operation of thinning and spreading bread.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Material idiomatic meaning is reported, but the source explicitly says the word's origin is unknown.
Pointer-only cross-reference with a lexical-variant comment.

cautions: The Lane material is matched through the contracted geminate root رق; the Quranic form identity, morphology, count, and location come from QAC.
The Quranic citation in Lane is preserved as lexical support for the parchment sense; no Lane bracketed citation has been converted into an additional modern verse location.
One idiomatic Form VI use is retained as ambiguous in the audit because its source explicitly says that the origin of the word is unknown.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: lane-unit:rqq:24081:g1:main reports the idiomatic meaning ‘to what state or choice one's mind will come’ but explicitly says that the origin of يَتَرَاقُّ is unknown; it is therefore represented as a cautious Classical meaning while marked AMBIGUOUS in the coverage ledger.
